description: Fresh post-Q3-tuning external blind compatibility benchmark for KOMPOSOS. Pair identities are separate from audit/blind_test_pairs.json, audit/ground_truth/*.json, prior audit/external_blind/*.json files, and audit/dev_compatibility/*.json.
selection_policy: Forty-two source-backed pairs selected from external papers, standards, handbooks, and public technical databases. Labels are evidence-backed compatibility outcomes, not outputs from KOMPOSOS. This file must not be used for bridge tuning; misses should define a separate development set before any successor blind benchmark is reported.
holdout_policy: Freeze with SHA256 before first diagnostic run. Do not change scorer logic against this file. If results are inspected and used for development, treat this benchmark as spent for future blind claims and freeze a new benchmark.

schema.expected_compatible: true means the pair is reported as usable/stable/standard under the cited context; false means reported incompatibility, decomposition, severe corrosion, immiscibility, or unsuitable direct interface.

pairs.citation: Nitta et al., Materials Today 2015, Li-ion battery materials and current collectors
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum foil is a standard positive-electrode current collector for oxide cathodes in passivating LiPF6 carbonate electrolytes.

pairs.citation: Aurbach et al., lithium metal deposition on copper current collectors in carbonate electrolytes
pairs.manual_source: Aurbach, Nonaqueous Electrochemistry, Marcel Dekker; lithium plating/stripping on copper collectors
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper is widely used as the low-potential collector/substrate for lithium deposition and stripping studies.

pairs.citation: Current collector review for lithium-ion batteries, Journal of Power Sources 2021
pairs.evidence_basis: Low-potential negative electrodes conventionally use copper current collectors; aluminum is reserved for positive-electrode service.

pairs.citation: Zhang, Journal of Power Sources 2006, copper dissolution at high positive potentials in Li-ion batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper current collectors dissolve at cathode potentials and are unsuitable for NMC positive-electrode collector service.

pairs.citation: Nitta et al., Materials Today 2015, Li-ion battery materials and current collectors
pairs.evidence_basis: Stainless steel is not the standard high-conductivity foil current collector for Li-ion cathode coatings.

pairs.citation: Current collector review for lithium-ion batteries, Journal of Power Sources 2021
pairs.evidence_basis: Graphite negative electrodes conventionally use copper collectors; aluminum is not the standard anode collector at graphite potentials.

pairs.citation: Tarascon and Armand, Nature 2001, issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: PVDF is a standard binder for lithium-ion positive-electrode composites, including oxide cathode systems.

pairs.citation: Small things make big deal: powerful binders of lithium batteries and post-lithium batteries, Energy Storage Materials 2019
pairs.evidence_basis: Fluoropolymer binders are chemically robust in lithium battery cathode composites.

pairs.citation: Mindemark et al., Progress in Polymer Science 2018, polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Unprotected PEO chemistry has inadequate oxidative stability for high-voltage oxide cathodes.

pairs.citation: Bresser et al., Energy & Environmental Science 2018, binder selection by electrode chemistry
pairs.evidence_basis: CMC/SBR aqueous binder systems are primarily negative-electrode binders, not default high-voltage NMC cathode binders.

pairs.citation: Bresser et al., Energy & Environmental Science 2018, binder selection by electrode chemistry
pairs.evidence_basis: SBR is associated with aqueous anode binder systems and is not the standard binder for high-voltage LCO cathodes.

pairs.citation: Tarascon and Armand, Nature 2001, issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: PVDF binder has been used broadly in lithium-ion composite electrodes, including graphite negative electrodes.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, polymer blend compatibility and polarity mismatch notes
pairs.evidence_basis: Nylon/PVC blends require tailored compatibilization because polarity, hydrogen bonding, and processing windows are mismatched.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, acetal and polyester blend compatibility notes
pairs.evidence_basis: POM and PET are not a standard miscible direct blend and have thermal/chemical mismatch without compatibilization.

pairs.citation: High-performance thermoplastic blend literature for PEEK/polyimide systems
pairs.manual_source: Utracki, Polymer Blends Handbook, Springer; high-performance polymer blend entries
pairs.evidence_basis: PEEK/polyimide high-performance engineering blends are reported for thermal and tribological property tuning.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, polyolefin and EPDM blend compatibility notes
pairs.evidence_basis: EPDM and polyethylene/polyolefin systems are used in thermoplastic elastomer and impact-modified blend families.

pairs.citation: Rubber compounding handbook literature on NR/SBR tire tread blends
pairs.manual_source: Mark, Erman, and Eirich, Science and Technology of Rubber, Elsevier
pairs.evidence_basis: Natural rubber/SBR blends are standard rubber compound systems.

pairs.citation: Hansen solubility parameter handbook and fluoropolymer compatibility notes
pairs.manual_source: Hansen, Hansen Solubility Parameters: A User's Handbook, CRC Press
pairs.evidence_basis: PTFE and PDMS have very poor direct miscibility and require special processing or fillers rather than simple polymer blending.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering; stainless/carbon steel joining guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Fe-base stainless and carbon steels are joinable with appropriate filler and corrosion design controls in non-corrosive service.

pairs.citation: ASM Specialty Handbook: Aluminum and Aluminum Alloys, 1993
pairs.evidence_basis: Same-base aluminum alloys can be mechanically joined with low galvanic mismatch when service design is appropriate.

pairs.citation: Copper Development Association, copper alloy families and joining guidance
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper-alloy family pairings have compatible base metallurgy and modest galvanic mismatch compared with dissimilar base metals.

pairs.citation: Special Metals and Haynes nickel alloy datasheets and joining guidance
pairs.evidence_basis: Nickel-base corrosion-resistant alloys are same-base alloy systems used in severe-service assemblies.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, galvanic corrosion guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Magnesium is highly anodic and has severe galvanic corrosion risk when coupled to passive stainless steel in conductive moisture.

pairs.citation: Corrosion Doctors, galvanic corrosion compatibility table
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum/copper direct contact has high galvanic corrosion risk in conductive environments.

pairs.citation: Non-oxide ceramic substrate and composite literature for AlN/SiC systems
pairs.manual_source: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: AlN and SiC are refractory non-oxide ceramics with compatible high-temperature substrate/composite contexts.

pairs.citation: Nitride ceramic composite processing literature for BN/AlN systems
pairs.manual_source: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: BN and AlN are nitride ceramic families used in high-temperature electrical and thermal management contexts.

pairs.citation: Janek and Zeier, Nature Energy 2016, solid electrolyte interfaces in all-solid-state batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Oxide/sulfide solid-electrolyte interfaces commonly suffer chemical and impedance mismatch without engineered interlayers.

pairs.citation: Hench, Journal of the American Ceramic Society 1998, bioceramics and bioactive glasses
pairs.manual_source: Hench, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 81(7), 1998; bioactive glass and hydroxyapatite composites
pairs.evidence_basis: Hydroxyapatite and bioactive glass are used together in bioactive ceramic composite and coating systems.

pairs.citation: Piezoelectric ceramic package and substrate literature for PZT on alumina
pairs.manual_source: Jaffe, Cook, and Jaffe, Piezoelectric Ceramics, Academic Press
pairs.evidence_basis: PZT ceramics are commonly integrated with alumina-type ceramic substrates and packages with controlled processing.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Zirconia and silicon carbide have large chemistry, thermal, and processing mismatch for direct co-sintered compatibility without engineered composites.

pairs.citation: Morkoc, Handbook of Nitride Semiconductors and Devices, 2008
pairs.evidence_basis: GaN-on-SiC wide-bandgap heterostructures are standard high-power and high-frequency semiconductor platforms.

pairs.citation: Morkoc, Handbook of Nitride Semiconductors and Devices, 2008
pairs.evidence_basis: AlN buffers and SiC substrates are used together in nitride semiconductor heterostructure platforms.

pairs.citation: Two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenide device literature on Si/SiO2 substrates
pairs.manual_source: Wang et al., Nature Nanotechnology 2012, electronics and optoelectronics of two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides
pairs.evidence_basis: Layered WS2 can be integrated on silicon/silicon-dioxide substrates through van der Waals or transfer processes.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: II-VI family membership does not overcome zincblende/wurtzite structural mismatch and large lattice/process mismatch.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: Same-family III-V chemistry is not sufficient when lattice and strain mismatch are too large for direct coherent heterostructures.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: InSb/InP has large lattice and thermal mismatch that prevents simple direct compatible heterostructure growth without specialized buffer schemes.

pairs.citation: Shelby, Introduction to Glass Science and Technology, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Borosilicate variants are same-family silica-borate glasses with compatible chemistry and broadly similar processing behavior.

pairs.citation: Hench, Journal of the American Ceramic Society 1998, bioceramics and bioactive glasses
pairs.manual_source: Hench, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 81(7), 1998; bioactive glass family compatibility
pairs.evidence_basis: 45S5 and S53P4 are related bioactive silicate glass families used in biomedical glass contexts.

pairs.citation: SCHOTT optical glass data sheets and optical glass catalog
pairs.evidence_basis: BK7 and fused silica are standard optical materials used in optically contacted or cemented assemblies under controlled process conditions.

pairs.citation: RP Photonics Encyclopedia, phosphate laser glass and silica glass material differences
pairs.evidence_basis: Phosphate laser glass and fused silica have different chemistry and thermal/process windows for direct fusion.

pairs.citation: RP Photonics Encyclopedia, fluoride and chalcogenide glass fiber material differences
pairs.evidence_basis: Fluoride and chalcogenide glasses have different chemical durability and processing windows for direct compatible fusion.

pairs.citation: SCHOTT optical glass data sheets and optical glass catalog
pairs.evidence_basis: Dense flint and crown optical glasses are catalog optical materials used in cemented lens assemblies with controlled adhesives/processes.
